facts: A Player Mode is a subscription app from Spry Labs that plays five roles for one person: Executive Coach, Executive Assistant, Chief of Staff, Accountability Partner and Cognitive Behavioral Mindset Coach.
The five roles are software made with AI, not people, and AI can be wrong, so you check anything important.
The A Player Mode web app at app.aplayermode.com works in any phone or computer browser today.
The iPhone app is waiting for App Store approval and the Google Play listing is coming soon.
Setup is about 3 minutes of easy-tap questions; it builds a Mind, Body, Spirit plan with your goals, your rules and your minimum day, and you approve each piece.
Every morning your plan is ready: one priority, a short start, then the day.
It turns a goal into a plan and the plan into one step a day.
After a missed day it gives you a minimum day with no catch-up, instead of piling the missed work onto tomorrow.
Radar catches promises you made before they are due.
Coaching comes one question at a time, with five one-tap coaching modes: High-Pressure, Executive Review, Recovery, Sprint and Deep Work.
Tracks are background filters that shape every plan, such as Operator Discipline, Strategic Patience and Resilience; the app suggests them and you approve them or switch them off.
It connects Google Calendar, Outlook calendar and mail, and the phone's own calendars; Gmail mail is planned and not connected yet.
Executive Roundtable costs $24.99 a month or $249.99 a year: all five roles plan and coach you, you do the last step, and it connects 1 calendar and 1 inbox.
The first 100 members (the Founding 100) pay $9.99 a month for as long as they stay subscribed; after that, Executive Roundtable is $9.99 a month for the first 3 months, then $24.99 a month.
Executive Suite costs $39.99 a month or $399.99 a year: it tracks birthdays, bills, renewals and appointments, drafts the replies you owe and proposes calendar fixes, and acts only when you tap yes.

Autopilot costs $79.99 a month or $799.99 a year: it carries out standing rules you set (sending follow-ups, moving flexible meetings, cancelling unused subscriptions), connects several calendars and inboxes, and keeps a daily done-list with undo.

It shows you every draft email or calendar change before it goes out, unless you turned on Autopilot for that kind of task, and buying a plan never switches a permission on: you turn each one on yourself.
It never spends your money: Autopilot can cancel a subscription you set a rule for, but it never buys, pays or transfers.
There is no free trial; plans renew until you cancel in the app's settings.
A Player Mode is not medical, mental-health, financial or legal advice, and it promises no income and no results.
